page.layout: One page of text in a single column; no margin notes. Running head at top centre; page number at top left.

main_text.p: Sule, Columna ; & sult, columnas] Hoc Saxonicum rylle, quod nobis manfit: felle enim, & ground-felle, nobis cujusvis structurae basis, vel fundamentum; magis autem specifice, magna trabs aedificio supposita ; Sax. alias znounopealle, h.e. substructio. Hinc nostratium felle. Belg. fuple, alias fuele, pro Limine. Limen autem Saxon. peopjrcpolve, alias Spnexpolo, unde nostrum thze-sholt.
Smerenne, Adipe] Hoc Saxonibus rmepre, de quo plura in Kuofmer.
Sneve, Nivis] Hoc Sax. rnap, unde nostrum snow, quod Belgis sneew: Teut. schnee.
main_text.head: Verba.
main_text.p: Scathan sal, Damnabit. Vide Be-scathot] Damnum Sax. rceaz: damnum faciens, rceapiz: innocens, unrceapiz. Hinc Graffator, eis rceapa: Piratici, rae-rceapaj? Hoc Belg. schaed, nobis hodie scatb, & scade: Unde Canem rapacem, a scadole (id est, scatb-full) curre dicimus. Saxonum rceapana rcnæpe, Latine sonat, Spelunca latronum.

page.notes: Several words in the Old English/Saxon and Belgic passages are set in black letter or a heavy type and are transcribed as best read; the Saxon forms are doubtful in places. The page is slightly faded at the right edge.
